provenance.citation: Colby, K.M., Weber, S., & Hilf, F.D. (1971). Artificial Paranoia. Artificial Intelligence, 2(1), 1-25. Colby's PARRY model: high-conviction beliefs (strength 1.0) trigger maximal defensive response (anger, fear, mistrust) when challenged by opposing-strength stimuli (strength 0.0).
provenance.locus: Section 3: Conflict detection — input strength conflicts with seeded belief strength by delta > 0.5 → paranoid defensive response.
provenance.notes: Six beliefs seeded at conviction 1.0. Six stimuli challenge each at strength 0.0, producing conflict=1.0 > 0.5, triggering 'defensive' response for each. All 6 candidates are eliminated. Trace has seed-beliefs + 6 defensive steps + affect-snapshot = 8 steps total.

expected.description: All 6 stimuli conflict with seeded beliefs at delta=1.0 > 0.5 → 6 defensive responses, 6 eliminated candidates. Colby PARRY 1971: maximum paranoid conflict triggers maximum defensive output.
